title: URL & URLSearchParams
lede: WHATWG URL parsing, query-string building, and route matching — the natural companions to fetch() for the REST-client priority. Parsing reuses libcurl's already-linked URL API rather than a hand-rolled parser. The recurring divergence is single-value-per-key: URLSearchParams is backed by a plain Map<string,string>, so a repeated key keeps only its last value and getAll() never returns more than one element. URLPattern is object-literal init only, and its exec() returns a merged Map rather than the spec's per-component result object.

entries.name: URL
entries.signature: new URL(url: string, base?: string): URL
entries.description: Parses an absolute URL into its component fields. Fields — href, protocol, host, hostname, port, pathname, search, hash, origin, username, password, searchParams — are plain object field reads, no dispatched methods, and href/protocol/host/hostname/port/pathname/search/hash/username/password are all settable (a setter re-parses and re-derives every field, matching Node; the combined `host` splits on the first `:` into hostname + port). A part absent from the URL reads back as "", matching real URL's own default. A malformed URL throws a catchable Error ("Invalid URL"). Parsing goes through libcurl's URL API rather than a hand-rolled parser.

params.name: url
params.desc: The URL to parse (absolute, or relative when a base is given).

params.name: base
params.desc: Optional base against which a relative url is resolved; an invalid base throws.

returns.desc: The parsed URL with its component fields.

entries.name: URLSearchParams
entries.description: Reads and builds query strings. new URLSearchParams() starts empty; new URLSearchParams(init) parses a query string and tolerates a leading '?', so passing a URL's own .search straight through just works. Backed by a plain Map<string,string>, so get/set/has/delete/size/keys()/values()/entries()/forEach() all come for free from the Map machinery, plus toString() (percent-encodes back into a query string) and getAll().

params.name: init
params.desc: Optional query string to parse (a leading '?' is tolerated).

entries.snippet:
const params = new URLSearchParams()
params.set("q", "hello world")
params.set("page", "2")
console.log(params.toString())  // q=hello%20world&page=2
differences: **Single value per key**: a repeated query-string key (`?a=1&a=2`) silently keeps only its last value — `.get()`/`.getAll()` never see the first one, so `.getAll()` never returns more than one element
There is no true multi-value `.append()`, since it can't be represented faithfully on top of the `Map<string,string>` backing structure

entries.name: URLPattern
entries.signature: new URLPattern(init?: { protocol?; hostname?; port?; pathname?; search?; hash?; username?; password? }): URLPattern
entries.description: WHATWG route matching. Each component pattern compiles once at construction to an anchored PCRE2 regex; .test/.exec match a full URL string, which parses via libcurl's URL API. An omitted init component defaults to "*" and reads back as such from the component fields. An unparseable input is false/null, never a throw; an invalid pattern throws a catchable TypeError at construction.
differences: Object-literal init only, over `protocol`/`hostname`/`port`/`pathname`/`search`/`hash`/`username`/`password` — no constructor-string form, no `baseURL`
Pattern grammar is literals, `\` escapes, `*`, `:name`, and `:name?` — `{}` groups, `+` modifiers, and inline `(regex)` groups throw a `TypeError` at construction

`.exec()` returns a merged `Map<string, string> | null` of every named group across components (an unset optional group is absent), not the spec's per-component `URLPatternResult` object — needs the deferred dynamic object model
`*` wildcards aren't exposed as numbered groups; no `hasRegExpGroups`

entries.name: url.parse()
entries.description: Node's legacy URL parser. Returns a Url object with the legacy field names (protocol, auth, host, port, hostname, hash, search, query, pathname, path, href), distinct from the WHATWG URL. Importable named, via namespace, or as the default of the url module.
entries.snippet:
import { parse } from 'url'
const u = parse('https://user:pw@example.com:8080/a?x=1#h')
console.log(u.host)      // example.com:8080
console.log(u.auth)      // user:pw
console.log(u.query)     // x=1
console.log(u.path)      // /a?x=1
differences: Absolute URLs only — a malformed/relative input throws `Invalid URL` (like `new URL()`), not Node's never-throw lenient object
An absent component is `""`, not Node's `null`
`slashes` and the `parseQueryString`-object form of `query` are not produced yet; `url.format`/`fileURLToPath` are separate follow-ons

entries.name: url.format()
entries.description: The inverse of url.parse: serializes a legacy Url object (or a WHATWG URL, or a plain object with the legacy fields) back into a URL string.
differences: The `options` argument is not supported; components are taken verbatim (no re-encoding)
A WHATWG URL argument serializes to its href

entries.name: url.fileURLToPath()
entries.description: Converts a file: URL (a string or WHATWG URL) into the percent-decoded POSIX filesystem path. Throws on a non-file: scheme.
differences: POSIX only; the options (windows) argument is unsupported
A non-localhost host is ignored, not rejected

entries.name: url.pathToFileURL()
entries.description: Resolves a path to absolute, percent-encodes it, and returns a WHATWG URL with the file: scheme.
entries.snippet:
import { pathToFileURL } from 'url'
console.log(pathToFileURL('/foo bar').href) // file:///foo%20bar
differences: POSIX only; the options argument is unsupported

entries.name: url.resolve()
entries.description: Resolves a target URL relative to a base URL (the new URL(to, from) resolution), returning the resulting string.
differences: Absolute bases only; a scheme-less base throws Invalid URL

entries.name: url.urlToHttpOptions()
entries.description: Remaps a WHATWG URL into the option object http.request accepts (protocol, hostname, path, port, auth, ...).
differences: Expects a WHATWG URL; a legacy Url/plain object isn't accepted

entries.name: url.domainToASCII() / domainToUnicode()
entries.description: Punycode/IDN conversion of a domain. Returns '' on failure, matching Node.
differences: IDN conversion of a non-ASCII domain needs the libcurl IDN backend (libidn2) — present on typical Linux, absent on the Mac build (returns '')
